s: Haoma is a Mazda-made
q: Praise to H(a)oma, Mazda-made. Good is H(a)oma, Mazda-made.

s: Haoma is good good (Mazda-made)
q: Good is H(a)oma, Mazda-made.

s: Haoma avails to the thousand-smiting of the D(a)êvas (the slightest tasting of thy juice)
q: The lightest pressure of thee, H(a)oma, thy feeblest praise, the slightest tasting of thy juice, avails to the thousand-smiting of the D(a)êvas.

s: Haoma causes healing (for those who caress him as a tender son)
q: Who as a tender son caresses H(a)oma, forth to the bodies of such persons H(a)oma comes to heal.

s: Haoma has healing virtues (whereby he is a healer)
q: Of all the healing virtues, H(a)oma, whereby thou art a healer, grant me some.

s: Haoma has victorious powers (whereby he is a victor)
q: Of all the victorious powers, whereby thou art a victor, grant me some.

s: Haoma causes friendship (through his stirring power)
q: but H(a)oma's stirring power goes hand in hand with friendship.

s: Haoma goes hand in hand with friendship (Homa's stirring power)
q: All other toxicants go hand in hand with Rapine of the bloody spear, but H(a)oma's stirring power goes hand in hand with friendship.

s: Haoma is associated with milk (when drunk mixed with milk)
q: the man who drinks thee mixed with milk

s: Haoma increases prosperity (when mixed with milk)
q: yea, more prosperous thou makest him, and more endowed with mind.

s: Haoma increases mind (when mixed with milk)
q: yea, more prosperous thou makest him, and more endowed with mind.

s: Haoma has exhilarations (vigorous, fresh, strong, bright, sparkling, and light)
q: let thine exhilarations go forth ever vigorous and fresh; and let them come to me with strong effect.

s: Haoma has Gâthas (holy)
q: These are thy Gâthas, holy H(a)oma

s: Haoma has songs (holy)
q: these thy songs

s: Haoma has teachings (holy)
q: and these thy teachings

s: Ahura Mazda possesses house (sanctified by H(a)oma)
q: within this house, Ahura's, which is sanctified by H(a)oma

s: Haoma has truthful ritual words (health-imparting and victory-giving)
q: and these thy truthful ritual words, health-imparting, victory-giving, from harmful hatred healing giving.

s: Gaini opposes Haoma (vainly attempting to foil him)
q: She vainly thinks to foil us, and would beguile both Fire-priest and H(a)oma

s: Kine is associated with food (food is requested for the Kine)
q: Food for the Kine, and pasture!

s: Kine is associated with pasture
q: Food for the Kine, and pasture!

s: Haoma causes progress
q: We worship the yellow lofty one; we worship H(a)oma who causes progress

s: Haoma advances settlements
q: who makes the settlements advance

s: Haoma drives away death
q: we worship H(a)oma who drives death afar

s: house is a sanctified house (Ahura's; sanctified by H(a)oma)
q: within this house, Ahura's, which is sanctified by H(a)oma

s: settlements advance progress (through H(a)oma)
q: who makes the settlements advance

s: Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma is a saint
q: And we worship (their) blessedness, and the Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma, the saint

s: cloud waters Haoma
q: I praise the cloud that waters thee

s: rains make grow Haoma (on the summits of the mountains)
q: and the rains which make thee grow on the summits of the mountains

s: birds carry Haoma (to high mountain places)
q: the bounteous birds have carried thee to the Peaks-above-the-eagles

s: good words belongs to saint (the speaker identifies with it)
q: of the good word am I, of the evil am I not

s: good deeds belongs to saint (the speaker identifies with it)
q: of the good deed am I, and of the evil, not.

s: Sraosha (Obedience) has speaker given to it the speaker
q: To Obedience am I given, and to deaf disobedience, not; to the saint do I belong, and to the wicked, not

s: Haoma sanctifies house
q: within this house, Ahura's, which is sanctified by H(a)oma

s: saint has speaker belonging to it Sraosha (Obedience)
q: To Obedience am I given, and to deaf disobedience, not; to the saint do I belong, and to the wicked, not

s: wicked is rejected by saint (the speaker does not belong to it)
q: to the saint do I belong, and to the wicked, not

s: Haoma is praised with Gâthas (with a Gâthic word)
q: Victory-giving smiteth H(a)oma, victory-giving is it worshipped; with this Gâthic word we praise it.

s: Haoma is poured from silver cup (into the golden chalice)
q: From the silver cup I pour Thee to the golden chalice over.

s: Haoma is poured into golden chalice (from the silver cup)
q: From the silver cup I pour Thee to the golden chalice over.

s: Haoma is a holy plant
q: This wide earth do I praise, expanded far (with paths), the productive, the full bearing, thy mother, holy plant!

s: Haoma has mother earth (productive and full bearing)
q: This wide earth do I praise, expanded far (with paths), the productive, the full bearing, thy mother, holy plant!

s: earth is a wide earth (productive and full bearing)
q: This wide earth do I praise, expanded far (with paths), the productive, the full bearing, thy mother, holy plant!

Ahura Mazda is a creator
q: The first of the good lands and countries which I, Ahura Mazda, created, was the Airyana Vaêgô, by the good river Dâitya.

s: the good river Dâitya is a river (good)
q: The first of the good lands and countries which I, Ahura Mazda, created, was the Airyana Vaêgô, by the good river Dâitya.

s: Angra Mainyu is a all death
q: Thereupon came Angra Mainyu, who is all death

s: Angra Mainyu counter creates the serpent in the river (by his witchcraft)
q: Thereupon came Angra Mainyu, who is all death, and he counter-created by his witchcraft the serpent in the river and winter, a work of the Daêvas.

s: Angra Mainyu counter creates fatal winters (by his witchcraft)
q: Thereupon came Angra Mainyu, who is all death, and he counter-created by his witchcraft the serpent in the river and winter, a work of the Daêvas.

s: fatal winters is a work of the Daêvas
q: Thereupon came Angra Mainyu, who is all death, and he counter-created by his witchcraft the serpent in the river and winter, a work of the Daêvas.

s: the plains in Sughdha is a good land and country (the second created)
q: The second of the good lands and countries which I, Ahura Mazda, created, was the plains in Sughdha.

s: the fly Skaitya brings death to cattle
q: the fly Skaitya, which brings death to the cattle.

s: the strong, holy Môuru is a good land and country (the third created)
q: The third of the good lands and countries which I, Ahura Mazda, created, was the strong, holy Môuru.

s: Ahura Mazda speaks to Zarathustra
q: Ahura Mazda spake unto Spitama Zarathustra, saying:

s: the beautiful Bâkhdhi with high-lifted banners is a good land and country (the fourth created)
q: The fourth of the good lands and countries which I, Ahura Mazda, created, was the beautiful Bâkhdhi with high-lifted banners.

s: Nisâya lies between the strong, holy Môuru (and Bâkhdhi)
q: was Nisâya, that lies between Môuru and Bâkhdhi.

s: Ahura Mazda makes dear the good lands and countries (to their dwellers)
q: I have made every land dear to its dwellers, even though it had no charms whatever in it

s: the burning of corpses is a sin for which there is no atonement
q: he counter-created by his witchcraft a sin for which there is no atonement, the burning of corpses.

s: Airyana Vaêgô is a good land and country (the first created)
q: The first of the good lands and countries which I, Ahura Mazda, created, was the Airyana Vaêgô

s: Airyana Vaêgô lies by the good river Dâitya
q: was the Airyana Vaêgô, by the good river Dâitya.

s: Airyana Vaêgô has ten winter months
q: There are ten winter months there, two summer months

s: Airyana Vaêgô has two summer months
q: There are ten winter months there, two summer months

s: Airyana Vaêgô has fatal winters (with the worst of its plagues)
q: Winter falls there, with the worst of its plagues.

s: Yima possesses golden ring (royal implement)
q: Then I, Ahura Mazda, brought two implements unto him: a golden ring and a poniard inlaid with gold. Behold, here Yima bears the royal sway!

s: Yima possesses poniard (inlaid with gold)
q: Then I, Ahura Mazda, brought two implements unto him: a golden ring and a poniard inlaid with gold. Behold, here Yima bears the royal sway!

s: Yima enlarges Earth (by three-thirds)
q: And Yima made the earth grow larger by three-thirds than it was before, and there came flocks and herds and men, at his will and wish, as many as he wished.

s: material world is subject to fatal winters (in the warning of Ahura Mazda)
q: Upon the material world the fatal winters are going to fall, that shall bring the fierce, foul frost; upon the material world the fatal winters are going to fall, that shall make snow-flakes fall thick, even an aredvî deep on the highest tops of mountains.

s: Earth is replenished with flocks and herds (under Yima's sway)
q: Thus, under the sway of Yima, three hundred winters passed away, and the earth was replenished with flocks and herds, with men and dogs and birds and with red blazing fires, and there was no more room for flocks, herds, and men.

s: Earth is enlarged by Yima (in successive expansions)
q: And Yima made the earth grow larger by three-thirds than it was before, and there came flocks and herds and men, at his will and wish, as many as he wished.

s: golden ring is a royal implement (used by Yima)
q: Then I, Ahura Mazda, brought two implements unto him: a golden ring and a poniard inlaid with gold. Behold, here Yima bears the royal sway!

s: Airyana Vaêgô contains the good river Dâitya (good river)
q: The Maker, Ahura Mazda, of high renown in the Airyana Vaêgô, by the good river Dâitya, called together a meeting of the celestial gods.

s: Ahura Mazda is highly renowned in Airyana Vaêgô (by the good river Dâitya)
q: The Maker, Ahura Mazda, of high renown in the Airyana Vaêgô, by the good river Dâitya, called together a meeting of the celestial gods.

s: the good river Dâitya is a good river (in Airyana Vaêgô)
q: The Maker, Ahura Mazda, of high renown in the Airyana Vaêgô, by the good river Dâitya, called together a meeting of the celestial gods.

s: celestial gods meet Ahura Mazda (in a meeting called by him)
q: The Maker, Ahura Mazda, of high renown in the Airyana Vaêgô, by the good river Dâitya, called together a meeting of the celestial gods.

s: fatal winters bring snow (fierce and foul frost)
q: Upon the material world the fatal winters are going to fall, that shall bring the fierce, foul frost; upon the material world the fatal winters are going to fall, that shall make snow-flakes fall thick, even an aredvî deep on the highest tops of mountains.

s: fatal winters cause death of cattle (all three sorts of beasts)
q: And all the three sorts of beasts shall perish, those that live in the wilderness, and those that live on the tops of the mountains, and those that live in the bosom of the dale, under the shelter of stables.

s: Vara is a abode for men (made by Yima)
q: Therefore make thee a Vara, long as a riding-ground on every side of the square, to be an abode for men; a Vara, long. as a riding-ground on every side of the square, to be a fold for flocks.

s: Vara is a fold for flocks (made by Yima)
q: Therefore make thee a Vara, long as a riding-ground on every side of the square, to be an abode for men; a Vara, long. as a riding-ground on every side of the square, to be a fold for flocks.

s: Vara contains water (flowing in a bed a hâthra long)
q: There thou shalt make waters flow in a bed a hâthra long; there thou shalt settle birds, by the ever-green banks that bear never-failing food.

s: Vara contains men and women (Vara) (of the greatest, best, and finest kinds)
q: Thither thou shalt bring the seeds of men and women, of the greatest, best, and finest kinds on this earth; thither thou shalt bring the seeds of every kind of cattle, of the greatest, best, and finest kinds on this earth.

s: Vara contains cattle (of the greatest, best, and finest kinds)
q: Thither thou shalt bring the seeds of men and women, of the greatest, best, and finest kinds on this earth; thither thou shalt bring the seeds of every kind of cattle, of the greatest, best, and finest kinds on this earth.

s: Vara contains trees (of the greatest, best, and finest kinds)
q: Thither thou shalt bring the seeds of every kind of tree, of the greatest, best, and finest kinds on this earth; thither thou shalt bring the seeds of every kind of fruit, the fullest of food and sweetest of odour.

s: Ahura Mazda is a Maker of the material world (most beneficent Spirit and Holy One)
q: O Ahura Mazda, most beneficent Spirit, Maker of the material world, thou Holy One!

s: Vara contains fruit (fullest of food and sweetest of odour)
q: Thither thou shalt bring the seeds of every kind of tree, of the greatest, best, and finest kinds on this earth; thither thou shalt bring the seeds of every kind of fruit, the fullest of food and sweetest of odour.

s: Vara excludes Angra Mainyu (brands stamped on mortal bodies)
q: There shall be no humpbacked, none bulged forward there; no impotent, no lunatic; no poverty, no lying; no meanness, no jealousy; no decayed tooth, no leprous to be confined, nor any of the brands wherewith Angra Mainyu stamps the bodies of mortals.

s: Angra Mainyu stamps bodies of mortals (with brands)
q: There shall be no humpbacked, none bulged forward there; no impotent, no lunatic; no poverty, no lying; no meanness, no jealousy; no decayed tooth, no leprous to be confined, nor any of the brands wherewith Angra Mainyu stamps the bodies of mortals.

s: Vara has nine streets (in its largest part)
q: In the largest part of the place thou shalt make nine streets, six in the middle part, three in the smallest.

s: Vara has six streets (in its middle part)
q: In the largest part of the place thou shalt make nine streets, six in the middle part, three in the smallest.

s: Vara has three streets (in its smallest part)
q: In the largest part of the place thou shalt make nine streets, six in the middle part, three in the smallest.

s: Vara is sealed with golden ring (and has a self-shining window)
q: That Vara thou shalt seal up with the golden ring, and thou shalt make a door, and a window self-shining within.

s: Vara is lit by uncreated lights (and created lights)
q: ‘There are uncreated lights and created lights. There the stars, the moon, and the sun are only once (a year) seen to rise and set, and a year seems only as a day.

s: Ahura Mazda teaches law of Mazda (to mortals)
q: The fair Yima, the great shepherd, O holy Zarathustra! he was the first mortal, before thee, Zarathustra, with whom I, Ahura Mazda, did converse, whom I taught the law of Ahura, the law of Zarathustra.

s: men and women (Vara) are born two per couple (a male and a female every fortieth year)
q: 'Every fortieth year, to every couple two are born, a male and a female. And thus it is for every sort of cattle. And the men in the Vara which Yima made live the happiest life.'

s: men and women (Vara) live happiest life (in the Vara)
q: 'Every fortieth year, to every couple two are born, a male and a female. And thus it is for every sort of cattle. And the men in the Vara which Yima made live the happiest life.'

s: Ahura Mazda converses with Yima (before Zarathustra)
q: The fair Yima, the great shepherd, O holy Zarathustra! he was the first mortal, before thee, Zarathustra, with whom I, Ahura Mazda, did converse, whom I taught the law of Ahura, the law of Zarathustra.

s: Yima is a mortal (first mortal to converse with Ahura Mazda)
q: The fair Yima, the great shepherd, O holy Zarathustra! he was the first mortal, before thee, Zarathustra, with whom I, Ahura Mazda, did converse, whom I taught the law of Ahura, the law of Zarathustra.

s: Yima is a great shepherd
q: The fair Yima, the great shepherd, O holy Zarathustra!

s: Yima is a son of Vîvanghat
q: 'Well, fair Yima, son of Vîvanghat, be thou the preacher and the bearer of my law!'

s: Yima rules material world (as king)
q: 'Yes! I will make thy worlds thrive, I will make thy worlds increase. Yes! I will nourish, and rule, and watch over thy world. There shall be, while I am king, neither cold wind nor hot wind, neither disease nor death.'

s: Earth feels sorest grief where burrows of the creatures of Angra Mainyu (where most such burrows exist)
q: It is the place wherein are most burrows of the creatures of Angra Mainyu.

s: Earth feels sorest grief where wife and children of one of the faithful (when driven along the way of captivity)
q: It is the place whereon the wife and children of one of the faithful, O Spitama Zarathustra! are driven along the way of captivity, the dry, the dusty way, and lift up a voice of wailing.

s: Earth digs out corpses of dogs and men
q: It is he who digs out of it most corpses of dogs and men.

s: Earth speaks to worshippers of Mazda (when he tills it with both arms)
q: He who would till the earth, O Spitama Zarathustra! with the left arm and the right, with the right arm and the left, unto him thus says the Earth: "O thou man! who dost till me with the left arm and the right, with the right arm and the left hither shall people ever come and beg (for bread), here shall I ever go on bearing, bringing forth all manner of food, bringing forth profusion of corn."

s: Ahura Mazda is a Maker of the material world (holy one)
q: O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One!

s: Ahura Mazda answers Zarathustra (in response to questions about the Earth and the law)
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'It is the place whereon one of the faithful steps forward, O Spitama Zarathustra! with the holy wood in his hand, the baresma in his hand, the holy meat in his hand, the holy mortar in his hand, fulfilling the law with love, and beseeching aloud Mithra, the lord of wide pastures, and Râma Hvâstra.'

s: worshippers of Mazda fulfills law of Mazda (with love and public beseeching)
q: It is the place whereon one of the faithful steps forward, O Spitama Zarathustra! with the holy wood in his hand, the baresma in his hand, the holy meat in his hand, the holy mortar in his hand, fulfilling the law with love, and beseeching aloud Mithra, the lord of wide pastures, and Râma Hvâstra.

s: worshippers of Mazda cultivates corn (in greatest amount)
q: It is the place where one of the faithful cultivates most corn, grass, and fruit, O Spitama Zarathustra! where he waters ground that is dry, or dries ground that is too wet.

s: worshippers of Mazda cultivates grass (in greatest amount)
q: It is the place where one of the faithful cultivates most corn, grass, and fruit, O Spitama Zarathustra! where he waters ground that is dry, or dries ground that is too wet.

s: worshippers of Mazda cultivates fruit (in greatest amount)
q: It is the place where one of the faithful cultivates most corn, grass, and fruit, O Spitama Zarathustra! where he waters ground that is dry, or dries ground that is too wet.

s: Earth feels happiest where worshippers of Mazda (where a faithful worshipper performs the law with love)
q: It is the place whereon one of the faithful steps forward, O Spitama Zarathustra! with the holy wood in his hand, the baresma in his hand, the holy meat in his hand, the holy mortar in his hand, fulfilling the law with love, and beseeching aloud Mithra, the lord of wide pastures, and Râma Hvâstra.

s: worshippers of Mazda is prohibited from carrying a corpse (alone by himself)
q: Let no man alone by himself carry a corpse. If a man alone by himself carry a corpse, the Nasu rushes upon him, to defile him, from the nose of the dead, from the eye, from the tongue, from the jaws, from the sexual organ, from the hinder parts.

s: worshippers of Mazda is cleansed by law of Mazda (from every evil thought, word, and deed)
q: In the same way the law of Mazda, O Spitama Zarathustra! cleanses the faithful from every evil thought, word, and deed, as a swift-rushing mighty wind cleanses the plain.

s: law of Mazda takes away sin (from one who confesses it)
q: The law of Mazda indeed, O Spitama Zarathustra! takes away from him who confesses it the bonds of his sin; it takes away (the sin of) breach of trust; it takes away (the sin of) murdering one of the faithful; it takes away (the sin of) burying a corpse; it takes away (the sin of) deeds for which, there is no atonement; it takes away the heaviest penalties of sin; it takes away any sin that may be sinned.

s: law of Mazda cleanses worshippers of Mazda (from every evil thought, word, and deed)
q: In the same way the law of Mazda, O Spitama Zarathustra! cleanses the faithful from every evil thought, word, and deed, as a swift-rushing mighty wind cleanses the plain.

s: corn is a food (when sown and eaten as part of material life)
q: What is the food that fills the law of Mazda? Ahura Mazda answered: ‘It is sowing corn again and again, O Spitama Zarathustra!

s: corn increases holiness (when sown)
q: He who sows corn, sows holiness: he makes the law of Mazda grow higher and higher: he makes the law of Mazda as fat as he can with a hundred acts of adoration, a thousand oblations, ten thousand sacrifices.

s: corn destroys fiends (when wheat is coming forth)
q: when wheat is coming forth, the Daêvas are destroyed. In that house they can no longer stay, from that house they are beaten away, wherein wheat is thus coming forth.

s: cultivation of the earth requires eating (for strength to do works of husbandry)
q: No one who does not eat, has strength to do works of holiness, strength to do works of husbandry, strength to beget children. By eating every material creature lives, by not eating it dies away.

s: burial of corpses has penalty punishments (when a corpse is not disinterred within half a year)
q: If a man shall bury in the earth either the corpse of a dog or the corpse of a man, and if he shall not disinter it within half a year, what is the penalty that he shall pay? Ahura Mazda answered: 'Five hundred stripes with the Aspahê-astra, five hundred stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.'

s: Earth feels happiest where house (where a priest, cattle, wife, children, and good herds are present and all thrive)
q: It is the place whereon one of the faithful erects a house with a priest within, with cattle, with a wife, with children, and good herds within; and wherein afterwards the cattle go on thriving, holiness is thriving, fodder is thriving, the dog is thriving, the wife is thriving, the child is thriving, the fire is thriving, and every blessing of life is thriving.

s: burial of corpses has atonement nothing (when a corpse remains buried into the second year)
q: For that deed there is nothing that can pay, nothing that can atone, nothing that can cleanse from it; it is a trespass for which there is no atonement, for ever and ever.

s: sin is removed by law of Mazda (when confessed and accompanied by resolve not to repeat the deed)
q: The law of Mazda indeed, O Spitama Zarathustra! takes away from him who confesses it the bonds of his sin; it takes away (the sin of) breach of trust; it takes away (the sin of) murdering one of the faithful; it takes away (the sin of) burying a corpse; it takes away (the sin of) deeds for which, there is no atonement; it takes away the heaviest penalties of sin; it takes away any sin that may be sinned.

s: sin is atoned for by repentance (when the sinner repents of all evil thoughts, words, and deeds)
q: The man here has repented of all his evil thoughts, words, and deeds. If he has committed any other evil deed, it is remitted by his repentance: if he has committed no other evil deed, he is absolved by his repentance, for ever and ever.

s: Earth feels happiest where cultivation of the earth (where dry ground is watered or overly wet ground is dried)
q: It is the place where one of the faithful cultivates most corn, grass, and fruit, O Spitama Zarathustra! where he waters ground that is dry, or dries ground that is too wet.

s: Earth feels happiest where herds (where there is most increase)
q: It is the place where there is most increase of flocks and herds.

s: Earth feels happiest where dung (where flocks and herds yield most)
q: It is the place where flocks and herds yield most dung.

s: Earth feels sorest grief where Arezûra (at its neck)
q: It is the neck of Arezûra, whereon the hosts of fiends rush forth from the burrow of the Drug.

s: Earth feels sorest grief where dead man (where most corpses of dogs and men lie buried)
q: It is the place wherein most corpses of dogs and of men lie buried.

s: Earth feels sorest grief where Dakhma (where most Dakhmas bearing corpses stand)
q: It is the place whereon stand most of those Dakhmas on which corpses of men are deposited.

s: Fargard IV is a fargard
q: Fargard IV.

s: field-contract is a contract (sixth of six kinds)
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They are six in number. The first is the word-contract; the second is the hand-contract; the third is the contract to the amount of a sheep; the fourth is the contract to the amount of an ox the fifth is the contract to the amount of a man the sixth is the contract to the amount of a field, a field in good land, a fruitful one, in good bearing.'

s: word-contract is redeemed by hand-contract (when made a mere word)
q: If a man make the word-contract a mere word, it shall be redeemed by the hand-contract; he shall give in pledge the amount of the hand-contract.

s: hand-contract is redeemed by sheep-contract
q: The hand-contract shall be redeemed by the sheep-contract; he shall give in pledge the amount of the sheep-contract.

s: sheep-contract is redeemed by ox-contract
q: The sheep-contract shall be redeemed by the ox-contract; he shall give in pledge the amount of the ox-contract.

s: ox-contract is redeemed by man-contract
q: The ox-contract shall be redeemed by the man-contract; he shall give in pledge the amount of the man-contract.

s: man-contract is redeemed by field-contract
q: The man-contract shall be redeemed by the field-contract; he shall give in pledge the amount of the field-contract.

s: contract-breaking is a sin (breaking a contract)
q: If a man break the word-contract, how many are involved in his sin?

s: contract-breaking has atonement multiple three hundred-fold (for breaking the word-contract)
q: His sin makes, his Nabânazdistas answerable for the three hundred-fold atonement.

s: contract-breaking has atonement multiple six hundred-fold (for breaking the hand-contract)
q: His sin makes his Nabânazdistas answerable for the six hundred-fold atonement.

s: Fargard IV has title Contracts and Outrages
q: Contracts and Outrages.

s: contract-breaking has atonement multiple seven hundred-fold (for breaking the sheep-contract)
q: His sin makes his Nabânazdistas answerable for the seven hundred-fold atonement!'

s: contract-breaking has atonement multiple eight hundred-fold (for breaking the ox-contract)
q: His sin makes his Nabânazdistas answerable for the eight hundred-fold atonement.

s: contract-breaking has atonement multiple nine hundred-fold (for breaking the man-contract)
q: His sin makes his Nabânazdistas answerable for the nine hundred-fold atonement.

s: contract-breaking has atonement multiple thousand-fold (for breaking the field-contract)
q: His sin makes his Nabânazdistas answerable for the thousand-fold atonement.

s: Nabânazdistas is answerable for atonement (for the offender's contract-breaking)
q: His sin makes, his Nabânazdistas answerable for the three hundred-fold atonement

s: Ahura Mazda is a Maker of the material world (Holy One)
q: O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! How many in number are thy contracts, O Ahura Mazda?

s: field-contract has penalty a thousand stripes (with each implement)
q: A thousand stripes with the Aspahê-astra, a thousand stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.

s: man (offender) steals the thing (when it is not restored after being asked for back)
q: He that does not restore (a thing lent), when it is asked for back again, steals the thing; he robs the man. So he does every day, every night, as long as he keeps in his house his neighbour's property, as. though it were his own.

s: man (offender) steals neighbour (lender) (by failing to restore borrowed property)
q: He that does not restore (a thing lent), when it is asked for back again, steals the thing; he robs the man.

s: Âgerepta is a act of rising to smite a man
q: If a man rise up to smite a man, it is an Âgerepta.

s: Avaoirista is a act of coming upon a man to smite him
q: If a man come upon a man to smite him, it is an Avaoirista.

s: Aredus is a act of smiting a man with evil aforethought
q: If a man actually smite a man with evil aforethought, it is an Aredus.

s: Peshôtanu is a offender (designation after the specified repeated or unatoned offense)
q: Upon the fifth Aredus he becomes a Peshôtanu.

s: Âgerepta has penalty five stripes (first occurrence, with each implement)
q: Five stripes with the Aspahê-astra, five stripes with the Sraoshô-karana; on the second Âgerepta, ten stripes with the Aspahê-astra, ten stripes with the Sraoshô-karana; on the third, fifteen stripes with the Aspahê-astra, fifteen stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.

s: Ahura Mazda answers questions about contracts
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They are six in number. The first is the word-contract; the second is the hand-contract; the third is the contract to the amount of a sheep; the fourth is the contract to the amount of an ox the fifth is the contract to the amount of a man the sixth is the contract to the amount of a field, a field in good land, a fruitful one, in good bearing.'

s: Avaoirista has penalty ten stripes (first occurrence, with each implement)
q: Ten stripes with the Aspahê-astra, ten stripes with the Sraoshô-karana; on the second Avaoirista, fifteen stripes with the Aspahê-astra, fifteen stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.

s: Aredus has penalty fifteen stripes (first occurrence, with each implement)
q: Fifteen stripes with the Aspahê-astra, fifteen stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.

s: Aspahê-astra is a implement of punishment
q: Three hundred stripes with the Aspahê-astra, three hundred stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.

s: Sraoshô-karana is a implement of punishment
q: Three hundred stripes with the Aspahê-astra, three hundred stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.

s: atonement is required for contract-breaking
q: If a man commit an Âgerepta and refuse to atone for it, what penalty shall he pay?

s: word-contract is a contract (first of six kinds)
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They are six in number. The first is the word-contract; the second is the hand-contract; the third is the contract to the amount of a sheep; the fourth is the contract to the amount of an ox the fifth is the contract to the amount of a man the sixth is the contract to the amount of a field, a field in good land, a fruitful one, in good bearing.'

s: water is a divine witness (brimstoned, golden, truth-knowing)
q: that deed which is done, when a man, knowingly lying, confronts the brimstoned, golden, truth-knowing water with an appeal unto Rashnu and a lie unto Mithra.

s: Fire is a witness to having received from his neighbour the ox or the garment (before the water)
q: Before the water and the blazing fire, O Spitama Zarathustra! let no one make bold to deny having received from his neighbour the ox or the garment (he has received from him).

s: meat fills man (offender) (much more than he who does not do so)
q: And of two men, he who fills himself with meat is filled with the good spirit much more than he who does not do so;

s: hand-contract is a contract (second of six kinds)
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They are six in number. The first is the word-contract; the second is the hand-contract; the third is the contract to the amount of a sheep; the fourth is the contract to the amount of an ox the fifth is the contract to the amount of a man the sixth is the contract to the amount of a field, a field in good land, a fruitful one, in good bearing.'

s: Ashemaogha is opposed by man (offender) (the ungodly one who does not eat)
q: it is this man that can strive against the ungodly Ashemaogha who does not eat.

s: Zarathustra is addressed by Ahura Mazda
q: Before the water and the blazing fire, O Spitama Zarathustra!

s: sheep-contract is a contract (third of six kinds)
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They are six in number. The first is the word-contract; the second is the hand-contract; the third is the contract to the amount of a sheep; the fourth is the contract to the amount of an ox the fifth is the contract to the amount of a man the sixth is the contract to the amount of a field, a field in good land, a fruitful one, in good bearing.'

s: ox-contract is a contract (fourth of six kinds)
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They are six in number. The first is the word-contract; the second is the hand-contract; the third is the contract to the amount of a sheep; the fourth is the contract to the amount of an ox the fifth is the contract to the amount of a man the sixth is the contract to the amount of a field, a field in good land, a fruitful one, in good bearing.'

s: man-contract is a contract (fifth of six kinds)
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They are six in number. The first is the word-contract; the second is the hand-contract; the third is the contract to the amount of a sheep; the fourth is the contract to the amount of an ox the fifth is the contract to the amount of a man the sixth is the contract to the amount of a field, a field in good land, a fruitful one, in good bearing.'

s: Ahura Mazda is a Maker of the material world
q: O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One!

s: Drug Nasu envelops them (with infection, pollution, and uncleanness)
q: how many of them does the Drug Nasu envelope with infection, pollution, and uncleanness?

s: Drug Nasu defiles ten (when the dead one is a priest)
q: If the dead one be a priest, the Drug-Nasu rushes forth, O Spitama Zarathustra! she falls on the eleventh and defiles the ten.

s: Drug Nasu defiles nine (when the dead one is a warrior)
q: If the dead one be a warrior, the Drug Nasu rushes forth, O Spitama Zarathustra! she falls on the tenth and defiles the nine.

s: sea Vouru-kasha is a sea
q: I, Ahura Mazda, send the waters from the sea Vouru-kasha down with the wind and with the clouds.

s: sea Pûitika is a sea
q: The waters stand there boiling, boiling up in the heart of the sea Pûitika,

s: sea Pûitika cleanses water (by boiling)
q: The waters stand there boiling, boiling up in the heart of the sea Pûitika, and, when cleansed there, they run back again from the sea Pûitika to the sea Vouru-kasha,

s: Dakhma receives corpse (for exposure)
q: then the worshippers of Mazda shall lay down the dead (on the Dakhma) his eyes towards the sun.

s: law of Mazda is a fiend-destroying law
q: This law, this fiend-destroying law of Zarathustra,

s: law of Zarathustra is a fiend-destroying law
q: This law, this fiend-destroying law of Zarathustra,

s: law of Zarathustra is greater than all other utterances (in greatness, goodness, and fairness)
q: so much above all other utterances in greatness, goodness, and fairness is this law, this fiend-destroying law of Zarathustra.

s: Ahura Mazda sends water from sea Vouru-kasha (with wind and clouds)
q: I, Ahura Mazda, send the waters from the sea Vouru-kasha down with the wind and with the clouds.

s: purity is a greatest good (next to life)
q: Purity is for man, next to life, the greatest good,

s: woman with child is confined enclosure (after delivering a still-born child)
q: On that place shall the worshippers of Mazda erect an enclosure, and therein shall they establish her with food, therein shall they establish her with clothes.

s: woman with child drinks gômêz (mixed with ashes, for three, six, or nine cups)
q: She shall drink gômêz mixed with ashes, three cups of it, or six, or nine, to wash over the grave within her womb.

s: woman with child remains separated for nine nights (after the first three nights)
q: Nine nights long shall she remain so: nine nights long, after the three nights have gone, shall she sit confined, and live separated from the rest of the worshippers of Mazda, as to her seat, her food, and her clothing.

s: still-born child is born to woman with child (during pregnancy)
q: if being a month gone, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven, or eight, or nine, or ten months gone, she bring forth a still-born child,

s: Ashemaogha is a wicked two-footed ruffian (ungodly)
q: that wicked, two-legged ruffian, that ungodly Ashemaogha,

s: Ashemaogha defiles creatures of the good spirit (while alive, directly and indirectly)
q: Whilst alive, indeed, O Spitama Zarathustra! that wicked, two-legged ruffian, that ungodly Ashemaogha, directly defiles the creatures of the good spirit, and indirectly defiles them.

s: corpse is eaten by bird (after death)
q: and it eats up the corpse of the dead man there:

s: corpse is laid on Dakhma (with the eyes toward the sun)
q: then the worshippers of Mazda shall lay down the dead (on the Dakhma) his eyes towards the sun.

s: water kills no man
q: Water kills no man: Astô-vîdhôtu ties the noose around his neck, and, thus tied, Vaya carries him off:

s: Ahura Mazda sends water to Dakhma
q: I, Ahura Mazda, make them stream down to the Dakhmas;

s: Mazdean house contains Fire (before a death occurs there)
q: When into our houses here below we have brought the fire, the baresma, the cups, the Haoma, and the mortar, O holy Ahura Mazda! if it come to pass that either a dog or a man dies there,

s: houses for the dead accommodate man (standing erect with limbs extended)
q: Large enough not to strike the skull, or the feet, or the hands of the man, if he should stand erect, and hold out his feet, and stretch out his hands: such shall be, according to the law, the houses for the dead.

s: houses for the dead hold lifeless body (for two nights, three nights, or a month)
q: And they shall let the lifeless body lie there, for two nights, or for three nights, or a month long, until the birds-begin to fly, the plants to grow, the floods to flow, and the wind to dry up the waters from off the earth.

s: bird feeds on corpse (after death)
q: then birds feed upon him, and chance brings him here, or brings him there.

s: Astō-vīdhōtu ties noose around man
q: Astô-vîdhôtu ties the noose around his neck, and, thus tied, Vaya carries him off:

s: Vaya carries off man (after Astō-vīdhōtu ties the noose)
q: Astô-vîdhôtu ties the noose around his neck, and, thus tied, Vaya carries him off:

s: gômêz is mixed with ashes (for purification)
q: She shall drink gômêz mixed with ashes, three cups of it, or six, or nine, to wash over the grave within her womb.

s: Ahura Mazda causes water to return to sea Pûitika (unseen)
q: then I, Ahura Mazda, make them flow back unseen; I, Ahura Mazda, make them flow back to the sea Pûitika.

s: gômêz is used with water (to cleanse the woman and her clothes)
q: she shall wash her body, she shall wash her clothes, with gômêz and water, by the nine holes, and thus shall she be clean.

s: Ahura Mazda rains plants down upon earth (to provide food and fodder)
q: Those plants, I, Ahura Mazda, rain down upon the earth, to bring food to the faithful, and fodder to the beneficent cow;

s: Zarathustra is a righteous
q: O righteous Zarathustra!

s: worshippers of Mazda construct houses for the dead (three small houses in every house and borough)
q: In every house? in every borough, they shall raise three small houses for the dead.

s: worshippers of Mazda lay dead on Dakhma (when birds begin to fly, plants grow, floods flow, and wind dries the waters)
q: then the worshippers of Mazda shall lay down the dead (on the Dakhma) his eyes towards the sun.

s: worshippers of Mazda wait before returning Fire (nine nights in winter and one month in summer)
q: They shall wait for nine nights in winter, for a month in summer, and then they shall bring back the fire to the house wherein the man has died.

s: Ahura Mazda is a Maker of the material world (as addressed by Zarathustra)
q: O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One!

s: Sraoshô-karana is used for punishments (as an instrument of stripes)
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They are Peshôtanus: two hundred stripes with the Aspahê-astra, two hundred stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.'

s: Drug Nasu defiles part of the water in a pond (with infection, pollution, and uncleanness)
q: What part of the water in a pond does the Drug Nasu defile with infection, pollution, and uncleanness?

s: corpse is removed by removal of corpses from water (when found in a stream of running water, pond, well, or snow or hail)
q: They shall, therefore, take the corpse out of the pond, and lay it down on the dry ground.

s: removal of corpses from water requires laying the corpse on dry ground (after taking it out of the water)
q: They shall, therefore, take the corpse out of the pond, and lay it down on the dry ground.

s: water is unclean until removal of corpses from water (when a corpse remains in it)
q: As long as the corpse has not been taken out of the water, so long shall that water be unclean and unfit to drink.

s: water becomes clean after removal of corpses from water (after part of the water has been drawn off where required)
q: after the corpse has been taken out and the water has been drawn off, the rest of the water is clean, and both cattle and men may drink of it at their pleasure, as before.'

s: well contains water (that is unclean while a corpse remains in it)
q: As long as the corpse has not been taken out of the water, so long shall that water be unclean and unfit to drink.

s: running stream is defiled within three steps down the stream, nine steps up the stream, six steps across (while a corpse remains in it)
q: ‘Three steps down the stream, nine steps up the stream, six steps across. As long as the corpse has not been taken out of the water, so long shall the water be unclean and unfit to drink.

s: running stream becomes clean after three stream flows (after the corpse has been taken out)
q: 'After the corpse has been taken out and the stream has flowed three times, the water is clean, and both cattle and men may drink of it at their pleasure, as before.'

s: Zarathustra is a holy Zarathustra (as addressed by Ahura Mazda)
q: A year long shall the ground lie fallow whereon dogs or men have died, O holy Zarathustra!

s: Haoma can be made clean clean (when touched by a corpse and strained for the Sacrifice)
q: It can, O holy Zarathustra! If it has been strained for the Sacrifice, no corpse that has been brought unto it, makes corruption or death enter it.

s: Haoma is defiled for four fingers (when not strained for the sacrifice and touched by a corpse)
q: If it has not been strained for the sacrifice, the stem is defiled the length of four fingers.

s: Haoma is buried in ground (the defiled four-finger length of stem, for a year)
q: That length of stem shall be buried in the ground, in the middle of the house, for a year long.

s: worshippers of Mazda secure corpse (by the feet and by the hair with brass, stones, or lead)
q: ‘There shall the worshippers of Mazda fasten the corpse, by the feet and by the hair, with brass, stones, or lead, lest the corpse-eating dogs and the corpse-eating birds shall go and carry the bones to the water and to the trees.

s: corpse-eating birds carry bones of the dead (if the corpse is not fastened)
q: If they shall not fasten the corpse, so that the corpse-eating dogs and the corpse-eating birds may go and carry the bones to the water and to the trees, what is the penalty that they shall pay?'

s: bones of the dead are kept in building (out of reach of the dog, fox, and wolf and where rain-water cannot stay)
q: ‘The worshippers of Mazda shall erect a building out of the reach of the dog, of the fox, and of the wolf, and wherein rain-water cannot stay.

s: building is built with stones, mortar, and earth (when the worshippers of Mazda can afford it)
q: Such a building shall they erect, if they can afford it, with stones, mortar, and earth;

s: worshippers of Mazda are subject to Peshôtanus (when they sow or water ground where dogs or men have died within a year)
q: 'They are Peshôtanus: two hundred stripes with the Aspahê-astra, two hundred stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.'

s: ground lies fallow for a year (whereon dogs or men have died)
q: A year long shall the ground lie fallow whereon dogs or men have died, O holy Zarathustra!

s: worshippers of Mazda may sow the rest of the ground (during the year that ground where dogs or men have died lies fallow)
q: A year long shall no worshipper of Mazda sow or water that part of the ground whereon dogs or men have died; he may sow as he likes the rest of the ground; he may water it as he likes.

s: worshippers of Mazda may water the rest of the ground (during the year that ground where dogs or men have died lies fallow)
q: A year long shall no worshipper of Mazda sow or water that part of the ground whereon dogs or men have died; he may sow as he likes the rest of the ground; he may water it as he likes.

s: sowing and watering ground is a sin (when performed within the year on ground where dogs or men have died)
q: 'If within the year they shall sow or water the ground whereon dogs or men have died, the sin is the same as if they had brought dead matter to the water, to the earth, and to the plants.'

s: ground is looked on for bones, hair, flesh, dung, or blood
q: 'They shall look on the ground for any bones, hair, flesh, dung, or blood that may be there.'

s: Aspahê-astra is used for punishments (as an instrument of stripes)
q: Ahura Mazda answered: 'They are Peshôtanus: two hundred stripes with the Aspahê-astra, two hundred stripes with the Sraoshô-karana.'

s: Fargard VII is a fargard
q: Fargard VII.

s: soul (dead man) leaves dead man (at death)
q: Directly after death, as soon as the soul has left the body

s: dog sees the corpse
q: On him she stays until the dog has seen the corpse or eaten it up

s: clothing is a covering (for infirm persons in a Mazdean house)
q: those clothes shall serve for their coverings and for their sheets, until they can withdraw and move their hands.

s: clothing is defiled by corpse (when touched by a corpse)
q: Can that garment be made clean, O holy Ahura Mazda! that has been touched by the carcase of a dog or the corpse of a man?

s: clothing is unfit for worshippers of Mazda (even after washing and cleansing)
q: Never can those clothes, even when washed and cleansed, be used either by a Zaotar, or by a Hâvanan, or by an Âtare-vakhsha, or by a Frabaretar, or by an Âbered, or by an Âsnâtar, or by a Rathwiskar, or by a Sraoshâ-varez, or by any priest, warrior, or husbandman.

s: gômêz purifies clothing (when not defiled with seed, sweat, dirt, or vomit)
q: But if it has not been defiled with seed, or sweat, or dirt, or vomit, then the worshippers of Mazda shall wash it with gômêz.

s: gômêz purifies woman with child (after delivering a still-born child)
q: She shall drink gômêz mixed with ashes, three cups of it, or six, or nine, to wash over the grave in her womb.

s: water purifies clothing (after washing with gômêz and rubbing with earth)
q: they shall wash it with water three times, and afterwards they shall expose it to the air for three months at the window of the house.

s: water is unclean when defiled by corpse (through improper corpse handling)
q: a corpse with filth into the waters, or unto the fire, and made either unclean

s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda (about death and ritual purity)
q: Zarathustra asked Ahura Mazda: 'O Ahura Mazda, most beneficent Spirit, Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! When a man dies, at what moment does the Drug Nasu rush upon him?'

s: worshippers of Mazda practice art of healing (when qualified through successful treatment of worshippers of the Daêvas)
q: If a worshipper of Mazda want to practice the art of healing

s: worshippers of the Daêvas are treated by art of healing (before worshippers of Mazda)
q: On worshippers of the Daêvas shall he first prove himself, rather than on worshippers of Mazda.

s: art of healing uses knife treatment (as one method of healing)
q: If he treat with the knife a worshipper of the Daêvas and he die

s: art of healing uses herbs (as one method of healing)
q: namely, one who heals with the knife, one who heals with herbs, and one who heals with the holy word

s: ground recovers after dead man (one year after the corpse lies exposed)
q: When the corpse of a dead man has lain on the ground for a year, clothed with the light of heaven, and beholding the sun, then the ground is itself again

s: Dakhma is a place where corpses are laid (built upon the face of the earth)
q: Those Dakhmas that are built upon the face of the earth, O Spitama Zarathustra! and whereon are laid the corpses Of dead men

s: Dakhma is occupied by fiends (as a place where troops of fiends gather)
q: that is the place where the fiends are, that is the place whereon the troops of fiends rush together

s: fiends feed on corpse (on Dakhmas)
q: On those Dakhmas, O Spitama Zarathustra! those fiends take food and void filth, (eating up corpses)

s: fiends cause diseases (through the stench arising from Dakhmas)
q: Thus from the Dakhmas arise the infection of diseases, itch, hot fever, humours, cold fever, rickets, and hair untimely white.

s: Ahura Mazda is a Maker of the material world (holy and most beneficent Spirit)
q: Ahura Mazda: 'O Ahura Mazda, most beneficent Spirit, Maker of the material world, thou Holy One!

s: woman with child gives birth to still-born child (at any stage from one to ten months)
q: If in the house of a worshipper of Mazda there be a woman with child, and if being a month gone, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven, or eight, or nine, or ten months gone, she bring forth a still-born child

s: still-born child requires enclosure (for the woman who delivers it)
q: On that place shall the worshippers of Mazda erect an enclosure, and therein shall they establish her with food, therein shall they establish her with clothes.
